title: Director Food Safety and Quality
text:
Job Summary
 
The Director, Food Safety & Quality is a senior, project-based individual contributor who is deployed to the most critical food safety and quality priorities across Maker’s Pride’s manufacturing network. Rather than leading a team, this leader goes where the need is greatest: stepping into facilities, programs, and issues that require immediate expertise, rapidly assessing the situation, and leading cross-functional teams to resolution without direct authority. Working in close partnership with plant leadership, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Product Development, Sanitation, and plant FSQA teams, the Director stabilizes high-risk areas, solves complex problems, and builds sustainable capability so improvements hold after the engagement ends. This role serves as a senior technical decision-maker on food safety risk and represents the company with regulators, key customers, and certification bodies on escalated matters.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 
Critical Site & Program Interventions
 

* Deploy to facilities, lines, and programs identified as highest risk or underperforming, often on short notice, to assess conditions and lead immediate stabilization.
* Rapidly diagnose root causes of food safety and quality gaps and develop clear, prioritized action plans with plant leadership.
* Lead cross-functional plant teams through execution of improvement plans, removing barriers and escalating risks as needed.
* Transition sustainable processes, tools, and ownership to site leadership before exiting each engagement.

Project Leadership & Prioritization
 

* Lead a portfolio of high-impact food safety and quality projects, defining scope, objectives, milestones, and success measures for each.
* Partner with the VP of HSE, FSQA to prioritize engagements based on enterprise risk, business impact, and customer or regulatory exposure.
* Manage multiple concurrent projects across sites, adjusting priorities quickly as new critical issues emerge.
* Provide regular project status, risk updates, and outcomes to the VP of HSE, FSQA and executive leadership.

Food Safety Risk Management & Decision-Making
 

* Serve as a senior technical decision-maker on food safety risk, including product hold, release, and disposition decisions.
* Lead or support the company’s response to food safety incidents, including recall and market withdrawal events, in partnership with senior leadership.
* Lead risk assessments and management of change reviews for high-risk changes to ingredients, processes, equipment, packaging, and facilities.
* Ensure HACCP, HARPC, and Preventive Controls programs at engaged sites are effectively designed, validated, and maintained.

**Technical Expertise:** Allergen Control, Sanitary Design & Complaints
 

* Address high-risk allergen control gaps, including labeling controls, scheduling, segregation, and cleaning validation and verification.
* Provide sanitary design expertise on critical equipment, facility, and capital projects, and ensure food safety requirements are incorporated.
* Lead investigations into significant or recurring customer and consumer complaints, driving root cause analysis and effective CAPA to closure.

External Relationships & Audit Readiness
 

* Represent Maker’s Pride with regulatory agencies, key customers, and certification bodies on escalated food safety matters.
* Lead sites through high-stakes regulatory inspections, customer audits, and GFSI-benchmarked certification audits (e.g., SQF, BRCGS), including remediation of findings.
* Support commercial teams in resolving critical customer quality concerns.

Sustainability & Network Learning
 

* Define success measures for each engagement and verify that improvements are sustained after transition.
* Capture lessons learned and translate solutions into standards, tools, and best practices that can be applied across the network.
* Identify systemic risks across engagements and recommend enterprise-level actions to prevent recurrence.

**Qualifications:** 
**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Engineering, Microbiology, Chemistry, Biological Sciences, or related discipline required.
 
 
**Experience:** 

* 10+ years of experience in food manufacturing, quality, engineering, or food safety required.
* Proven track record leading critical, high-visibility projects or turnarounds across multiple manufacturing sites required.
* Working knowledge of FSMA, HACCP, Preventive Controls, GMPs, and GFSI-benchmarked standards (SQF, BRCGS, or similar) required
* Experience with sanitary design principles and capital project support preferred
* Experience with quality management systems and data analysis tools preferred

**Certifications:** PCQI and/or HACCP certification and Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or equivalent continuous improvement certification preferred
 
 
**Skills:** 

* Strong root cause analysis and data analysis skills, with the ability to quickly assess complex, ambiguous situations and determine what matters most.
* Ability to scope, prioritize, and execute multiple concurrent projects across sites, adjusting quickly as critical issues emerge.
* Builds trust and credibility quickly with plant teams, executives, customers, and regulators to drive results with teams that do not report to them.
* Strong written and verbal communication at all levels, and comfortable shifting between sites, projects, and priorities in a high-travel role.

Work Environment & Physical Demands
 

* 70% travel to manufacturing facilities
* Work in manufacturing environments that may include exposure to noise, varying temperatures, allergens, and moving equipment.
* Ability to stand and walk for extended periods, climb stairs and ladders, and carry light loads.
* Must comply with all GMP, food safety, and safety requirements, including use of required personal protective equipment.

The information provided in this document provides an overview of the most common duties, qualifications, and demands of the position. It is not intended to be a comprehensive summary of the role, and the duties, qualifications, and demands of the position are subject to change without notice. The expectations provided here may also be modified if an employee with a disability could effectively meet the expectations for the role with reasonable accommodation.
 
The pay range for this full-time, salaried position is $141,436-$212,154/year. Individual base pay depends on work location and additional factors such as experience, job-related skills, and relevant education or training. The position is eligible for a discretionary annual incentive based on company and individual performance. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, 401k and wellness benefits beginning on the first day of employment.
 
 
Maker's Pride is an Equal Opportunity Employer.
